## Summary

**BSEL** (Bit Select): Bitwise selection from &lt;vea&gt; , taken if b=1.

## Details

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Operation | `64x b=1 ? then a → d` |
| Syntax | `BSEL <vea>,mask,d` |
| Short | Bitwise selection from &lt;vea&gt; , taken if b=1 |
| Description | Masked bits are taken from &lt;vea&gt; , unmasked stays d. This instruction allows a bit-by-bit selection of data from two sources into the destination. Typically, this is applied in conjunction with a prior pcmp instruction. |
| Condition codes | not affected |

### Encoding

| Word | Bits | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15–9 | `1111111` |
| 1 | 8 | A |
| 1 | 7 | B |
| 1 | 6 | D |
| 1 | 5–3 | Mode |
| 1 | 2–0 | Register |
| 2 | 15–12 | b(mask) |
| 2 | 11–8 | d |
| 2 | 7–0 | `00101001` |

### Example

```asm
    bsel    d0,d1,d2
```

```text
vea d0: 01 23 45 67 89 AB CD EF
b d1: 00 0F FF C0 00 CF FF F0
d d2: 55 55 55 55 55 55 55 55
Result:
d d2: 55 53 45 55 55 9B CD E5
```

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- The 68000–68060 have no BSEL. It is new on the 68080.

## Do / Don't

- No rules beyond the details above.
